name: Pediatric arthroscopic approach to the proximal tibia
aliases: pediatric knee arthroscopy for epiphyseal fracture
corridor: Standard anterolateral viewing and anteromedial working portals beside the patellar tendon, with restrained irrigation because extravasation can cause compartment syndrome

positioning.text: Position so the medial and lateral soft spots beside the patellar tendon can be used and the knee fully examined.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the patellar tendon and the medial and lateral soft spots adjacent to it.

incision.text: Make a 5 mm stab at the lateral soft spot for the camera and a 5 mm medial stab for a hook.

superficial_interval.text: Insert the trocar and sleeve carefully to avoid articular cartilage, then exchange for the arthroscope.

deep_interval.text: Irrigate until the joint is clear. Continuous pump irrigation may help, but extravasation through a ruptured capsule can cause compartment syndrome. Examine the whole joint for meniscal, ligament, and osteochondral injury.

layers.text: Skin, portal tracks beside the patellar tendon, capsule, then the joint and epiphyseal fracture.

structures_at_risk.text: Articular cartilage at portal entry and the compartments of the leg if irrigation extravasates are at risk.

danger_zones.text: A ruptured capsule plus high-pressure irrigation is the compartment-syndrome danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not force the trocar against cartilage.

exposure.text: Allows visualization and manipulation of a minimally or nondisplaced epiphyseal fracture and a full intra-articular survey.

limitations.text: Only for minimally or nondisplaced patterns, or to check reduction quality. Advanced arthroscopic experience is required.

indications.text: Used for selected pediatric epiphyseal fractures that can be seen and handled through standard AM/AL portals.

complications.text: Complications include cartilage scuffing and compartment syndrome from fluid extravasation.

procedure_applications.condition: A minimally or nondisplaced epiphyseal fracture is visualized or reduced arthroscopically by an experienced surgeon

questions.question: Which portals are used?
questions.answer: Anterolateral viewing and anteromedial working portals beside the patellar tendon.

questions.question: What extra pediatric irrigation risk is emphasized?
questions.answer: Fluid extravasation that may lead to compartment syndrome, especially if the capsule is ruptured.

questions.question: When is arthroscopy recommended?
questions.answer: Only for minimally or nondisplaced fractures, or to evaluate reduction, by an experienced arthroscopist.
